payload.analysis: Postoperative pathology confirms poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (diffuse type) with serosal/pancreatic invasion, vascular/perineural invasion, and 8/51 positive nodes (pT4bN3a), confirming gastric cancer. payload.report: The initial gastroscopy found antral lesions, raising suspicion of gastric cancer versus benign ulcer/polyp. Clinical course—radical distal gastrectomy, adjuvant chemotherapy, and radiotherapy—strongly favored malignancy. Definitive postoperative pathology confirmed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with serosal/pancreatic invasion, vascular tumor thrombus, perineural invasion, duodenal involvement, and 8/51 positive lymph nodes (pT4bN3a), which is the gold-standard evidence for gastric cancer. Molecular testing showing HER2 amplification with intact MMR further corroborates malignancy. Benign ulcer/polyp is refuted by invasive features, lymph node metastases, and oncologic treatment. Thus, the frontier is sufficiently refined: gastric malignant tumor is confirmed with 0.99 confidence, directly answering the core question.
